comparator.name: Global Law
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg's current curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, publishes 60 ECTS of mandatory study in years 1 and 2. Year 3 contains a 30-ECTS mobility window with seven approved options, followed by 30 ECTS of mandatory courses and thesis work. Because the generic bachelor does not designate one mobility option as the representative route, the comparison preserves that structured choice as a 30-ECTS component rather than selecting a minor for UCR fit. Zero-credit communication-skills and mentoring activities are noted by Tilburg but excluded from the 180 credited ECTS. The credited components total exactly 180 ECTS.
components: Introduction to Philosophy of Global Law
Mobility Window: one approved exchange or minor option

One 30-ECTS option is required from exchange/study abroad, Global Law and Business, Dutch Law, Law and a Sustainable Future, another Tilburg minor, a minor at another Dutch university, or a free minor.
Compulsory independent bachelor thesis concluding the programme.

candidates.label: Dutch law and preparation for Dutch legal practice
candidates.reason: Tilburg's Dutch Law minor requires Dutch-language constitutional-rights, property, contract, criminal-liability and civil-procedure courses and C1 Dutch. UCR offers comparative legal study but no Dutch-language doctrinal or procedural sequence capable of sustaining a distinct 24-course Dutch qualifying-law curriculum.

alternatives.label: Global and comparative law, institutions & justice
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines comparative, international, EU, constitutional, criminal and private law with political institutions, sociology, ethics, legal argument, cross-border commerce and global justice. It cannot reproduce Tilburg's complete doctrinal sequence, specialist legal-skills courses or required legal thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains UCR's complete available law sequence alongside comparative politics, international relations, sociology, ethics, communication and justice; the label describes that interdisciplinary composition without implying an LLB or qualifying law degree.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes every formally dependent law course, and Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law. Legal, political, sociological and communication foundations precede upper-level EU politics, private law, social theory and persuasive communication. All courses are offered in their assigned terms and all formal prerequisites are completed earlier.

alternatives.label: Commercial law, business & global regulation
alternatives.concept: A commercial-law direction connecting private, international, constitutional and EU law with transnational business law, accounting, finance, economics, strategy, corporate governance, negotiation and applied business research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme combines five law courses with a sustained business, finance, economics, governance, negotiation and research sequence; the label accurately signals a commercial and regulatory direction rather than a general law degree.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal law, international-relations theory, EU politics, peace and conflict, ethics, qualitative sociology, environmental justice and legal-history context. It adds accounting, finance, econometrics, market research, digital strategy, organisational psychology, negotiation and international business governance. Twelve of 24 courses differ.
progression: Law, Society & Justice and Business Foundations establish the legal and commercial strands. Research Methods & Statistics precedes organisational psychology, negotiation, public economics, econometrics and market research. Business Foundations also precedes strategy, transnational business law, finance and international governance. All assigned offerings are present and all formal prerequisites occur earlier.

alternatives.label: Law, sustainability & environmental governance
alternatives.concept: A law-and-sustainability direction linking international, EU, constitutional, criminal, private and human-rights law to environmental governance, public economics, climate justice, water, resources, circularity, media and applied sustainability research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme retains a substantial comparative-law core while sustainability foundations, environmental governance, justice, water, resources, circularity and applied research form a coherent second strand.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces commercial law, international-relations theory, sociology, legal communication, ethics and legal-history context with sustainability foundations, Earth systems, water, resources, circularity, public economics, environmental media and applied sustainability research. Eleven courses differ from the closest match and fourteen from the commercial route.
progression: Law and Sustainability Essentials I precede their advanced legal and sustainability sequences; Sustainability Essentials II precedes circular-resource and Earth-resource courses. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Public Economics. Foundational politics, economics and environmental study precede upper-level EU politics, governance and applied research. Every assigned offering and prerequisite passes.

establishes the economic context in which sustainability rules and policy instruments operate

blocks: Legal foundations, history, philosophy and research
Both introduce legal fields and the operation of law; UCR is comparative and interdisciplinary rather than an LLB foundation sequence.
Both develop normative reasoning about justice, though UCR teaches general ethics rather than specialist global jurisprudence.
UCR supplies global social histories of rights and power, but not a dedicated legal-history survey.
Both develop research design and evidence evaluation; UCR's course is broader and quantitative.
No scheduled UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg's second programme-specific global-law introduction.
UCR distributes perspectives on law across law, politics, sociology and philosophy rather than one dedicated course.
UCR Ethics does not reproduce advanced philosophy of global law.
UCR offers an optional independent research element, but the scheduled programme does not require Tilburg's 12-ECTS legal thesis.
Public, international, European and criminal law
Both examine criminal liability and justice; UCR is comparative and less doctrinally extensive.
Both cover sources, subjects and major fields of public international law.
Both study constitutional limits on public authority; UCR compares multiple systems.
Both address EU institutions, sources, rights, market rules and enforcement.
Comparative politics supplies institutional context but does not reproduce administrative-law doctrine.
Sociology supports analysis of crime and institutions but is not a dedicated criminology course.
UCR international law and history courses do not reproduce a dedicated history of international law.
UCR covers cross-border public and commercial questions but has no dedicated conflict-of-laws course.
Private law, commerce, business and regulation
Both address obligations and private-law relationships; UCR offers one broad principles course.
Both address commercial transactions and disputes; UCR has an explicitly transnational scope.
Both provide business foundations for legal-commercial analysis, though UCR is not designed specifically for lawyers.
UCR examines AI governance and regulation in business, but not the full breadth of law, technology and society.
Finance addresses firms, creditors and risk but does not reproduce property and insolvency doctrine.
International business governance complements corporate law without reproducing its doctrine.
UCR private and criminal law discuss liability, but no scheduled course directly reproduces Tilburg's dedicated Tort Law course.
UCR has no second advanced obligations-and-contract law course.
Sustainability, environmental governance and structured choice
Tilburg's 30-ECTS mobility window remains a structured external choice; UCR alternatives instead show three fixed interdisciplinary curricula.

selection.assessment: The closest programme captures the global and comparative legal core with explicit limits on doctrinal depth and thesis work. Official programme-specific minors support two further coherent directions: global commercial law and business, and law with sustainability. Their completed curricula differ pairwise by at least eleven courses. The separately evidenced Dutch-law direction is infeasible because UCR lacks the required Dutch-language doctrinal and procedural sequence. Production therefore reaches the maximum of three alternatives.

notes.text: UCR offers a substantial interdisciplinary law curriculum but not Tilburg's 180-ECTS LLB, specialist legal-skills sequence, required legal thesis or Dutch qualifying-law route. These pathways should not be read as qualifying law degrees.
